rows.subtype: Approach: learn basic first aid and keep emergency numbers ready [Thinking]

rows.subtype: Approach: report to the police and insurer with the right documents [Action]
rows.description: After a serious collision the driver files a report, informs the insurer within the stated time and keeps hospital bills and photos. Following the formal process protects claims.

rows.subtype: Approach: leave the scene out of fear [Pitfall]
rows.description: Panicking and afraid of a crowd, a driver flees after hitting a pedestrian. Fear overrides duty, worsens legal trouble and denies help to the injured person.

rows.subtype: Approach: follow official warnings and evacuation orders [Action]
rows.description: When flood alerts are issued for a river town, a student checks the district authority and weather department updates and moves to a designated shelter early. Official information beats rumours.

rows.subtype: Approach: prepare a go-bag and family meeting point in advance [Action]
rows.description: The person packs documents in a waterproof bag, a torch, a charged power bank, water and basic medicines for family use, and agrees on a meeting place. Preparation removes hesitation.

rows.subtype: Approach: wait and see because it may not be serious [Pitfall]
rows.description: Having seen earlier warnings pass with little harm, the person stays put until water enters the ground floor. Normalcy bias delays leaving until the routes are cut.

rows.subtype: Approach: scenario planning for power and phone loss [Thinking]
rows.description: The person imagines being cut off for two days and plans for a paper list of numbers, a radio or offline map, and a shared plan on who contacts whom. Contingency thinking covers what technology may not.

rows.subtype: Approach: help neighbours through community coordination [Action]
rows.description: After moving to safety, the student joins a local volunteer group, and works with the authorities to deliver food and check on elders. Coordinated help is safer than individual risky acts.
